newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sri Lanka central bank sees FRN setting benchmark.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka central bank sees FRN setting benchmark.

text.p: Sri Lanka's first floating rate note issue in 15 years will set a benchmark for the country's private sector borrowers, Central Bank Governor A.S. Jayawardena said on Thursday.
"We are coming in with this small FRN, more or less, to set the benchmark for private sector issuers in Sri Lanka," Jayawardena told Reuters Financial Television.

Sri Lanka plans to launch a US$50 million FRN in March. Citibank International and ING Barings are joint lead managers of the issue, which will have a final maturity of three years and a put option on the second anniversary.
Roadshows for the issue began on Thursday in Hong Kong. Presentations also will be made in London and Bahrain.

Jayawardena said he does not see the issue heralding more active participation by the Sir Lankan government in the international capital markets because the country continues to raise concessionary funding from multilateral agencies.
Rather, the central bank governor said he hopes the issue will be an incentive for the private sector to raise money for much-needed infrastructure investment.

"We have a large amount of infrastructure investment that has to be done in transport, energy and telecommunications. And these will be encouraged with local and foreign private sector investment," he said.
He said the US$50 million raised will supplement a US$20 million grant from the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank for infrastructure development.
Development of alternative forms of power generation is particularly important because of the country's heavy reliance on hydropower, he said.
Jayawardena noted that Sri Lanka has posted growth rates of five to six percent over the last few years despite the ethnic warfare that has scarred the country.
"Despite the fact that we've had some problems in the northern part of the country, the private sector in the rest of the economy is doing extremely well," Jayawardena said.
